name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Austin Scott seeking re-election with large financial edge
Democratic challenger has minimal fundraising and no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: Austin Scott holds a heavily Republican district with a decisive money advantage, while Kelly Esti has raised almost nothing and drawn no outside spending. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican win, so the forecast stays near the baseline with a slight nudge toward Scott.
model.watch: A sudden influx of outside spending against Scott or a major scandal would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 8th District leans Republican by about fifteen points, and incumbent Austin Scott is running for re-election with a well-funded campaign. He has raised over $1.1 million and holds more than $1.3 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised under $20,000 and has essentially no cash remaining. No outside groups are spending meaningfully in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this contest, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency and money advantages, and prediction markets, which price Scott's win probability at roughly 95 percent. The expected result is a comfortable Republican victory in the mid-to-high teens, with low but nonzero uncertainty given the absence of polling.
